params.body:
Closes #996

Replaces #999, which went red on "Changed PHP is formatted" over the spacing in its new test file (pint's `concat_space` and `binary_operator_spaces`). Same change, rebased on main of today, the test file formatted by pint, the targeted tests and the full suite run again. #999 can be closed.

A garage replaced its logo on the garage sheet. Its quotes and order forms showed the new logo, its showroom still the old one (Portal mail 15, 12 October 2026).

## Why

The logo was stored as `{dealer}.{ext}`, so a replacement with the same extension landed on the same name and `dealers.image` did not change. Two readers key on that name:

- The showroom screen loads the logo through `dealer.index.image`, whose URL is the file name and which answers with a one-day `Cache-Control`. A TV that has been running the showroom, or a browser that opened it before, keeps the old bytes for a day.
- The downloaded slides hash the dealer's `image` name in `ShowroomSlide::fingerprint`, not its bytes, so every cached slide (`ShowroomSlideCache`) read as "unchanged" and the zip kept shipping the old logo until the vehicle's own data changed.

The PDFs read the bytes from the disk on every render (`PdfImage::src`), which is why they were right.

## What changes

- `DealerController::upload()` names the file `{dealer}-{10 hex of sha1(bytes)}.{ext}`. A replacement is a new URL for the screen and a new fingerprint for the slides, without touching the cache rules. The new file is written before the previous one is deleted, so a failed upload leaves the dealer with the logo it had; the legacy `{dealer}.{ext}` is removed as well. Uploading the same bytes again keeps the same name and does not delete the file.
- `DealerController::update()` keeps the two uploaded files (`image`, `attachment`) out of the row data. They went in before: the logo was written to `dealers.image` as its temporary upload path first, so `upload()` read that path as "the previous logo" and the real previous file stayed behind.
- Rule R S2-7.16 says how the logo file is named since today and what went wrong before.
- `AReplacedLogoIsANewFileTest`: a replacement is a new name, the previous file and the legacy name go, the fingerprint changes, the new URL serves the new (blue, not red) logo; a second replacement again; the same bytes again keep their file.

## Checks

- `AReplacedLogoIsANewFileTest`, `DealerLogoTest`, `ShowroomSlideTest`, `DealerAuthorizationTest`, `CarpassPasswordTest`, `GarageAdministrationIsForAdministratorsTest`, `DelegationTest`: 73 tests green.
- PHPStan: no errors.
- Pint on the new test file: green.
- Full suite on the workbench: 3047 tests, all green except the six cases of `APhotoWithoutAForegroundIsNotAFaultTest`, which fail identically on the other branch of this mail (a `Log::warning` count in the photo-answer flow, which this change does not touch; known to fail on a reused local test database).

## After the merge

The garages whose logo is still wrong on the showroom need nothing from us except a new upload of the logo on the garage sheet (the current file keeps its old name until then); after that the showroom screen picks it up on its next reload and "Opnieuw maken" redraws the slides.
params.title: A replaced garage logo is a new file under a new name
